mainTopic: Hadrianic earthenware and using forbidden objects for other purposes (רוצה בקיומו), plus beer-vinegar, the רבן גמליאל testimony, and עורות לבובין
overview: The גמרא first rules that vinegar made from Aramean beer is forbidden because יין נסך yeast is mixed in, though רב אשי permits vinegar from a storeroom. It then explains the משנה's חרס הדרייני: shards of jugs from הדריינוס קיסר's vineyard that soaked up so much wine that people soaked the shards in water and drank it. Next it asks whether one may use these shards to prop up a bed, which is a case of wanting a forbidden thing to stay whole for another use (רוצה בקיומו). רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן argue, and the הלכה follows the one who forbids. A ברייתא forbidding donkey blankets made from non-Jewish wineskins seems to challenge the permitting view, but רבא explains that the wineskin rule is a separate decree against patching. The forbidding view explains that jugs may be traded because no real forbidden wine is in them, unlike the shards. The גמרא then settles two conflicting reports of שמעון בן גודא's testimony about רבן גמליאל. Finally, it begins defining עורות לבובין, hides torn opposite the heart.

steps.title: Vinegar from Aramean beer is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Vinegar made from Aramean beer is אסור because they mix yeast from יין נסך into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Vinegar made from Aramean beer is forbidden, because they mix into it yeast from wine used for idol worship.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states a rule: vinegar made from Aramean beer is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beer itself is not a wine product. The problem is that the Arameans add wine yeast (דורדיא) taken from יין נסך into it, and that mixture makes the vinegar forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured for idol worship, forbidden for any benefit

phrases.english: This vinegar made of Aramean beer is forbidden,
because they mix into it yeast of libation wine.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Aramean beer-vinegar is forbidden because of mixed-in יין נסך yeast.

steps.title: רב אשי permits vinegar from a storeroom
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says vinegar taken from a storeroom is permitted, because if yeast were mixed in, it would spoil over time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: But vinegar from a storeroom is permitted, since if they mixed yeast into it, it would spoil.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי adds a limit to the previous rule: vinegar that comes from a storage house is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban in step 1 depends on yeast actually being mixed in. Vinegar meant for long storage cannot have yeast added, because it would rot. So we can assume stored vinegar has no יין נסך in it.

keyTerms.meaning: Storeroom, a place for long-term storage

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
But from a storeroom it is permitted,
since if they mix yeast into it, it would spoil.
phrases.notes: So stored vinegar can't have that yeast in it. Otherwise it would go bad sitting in storage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the ban of step 1 to vinegar not from a storeroom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Vinegar from a storeroom is permitted.

steps.title: What is Hadrianic earthenware?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's term חרס הדרייני and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'and Hadrianic earthenware' is forbidden. What is Hadrianic earthenware?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new phrase in the משנה and asks for its meaning. This sets up the explanations that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists חרס הדרייני among forbidden items without explaining it. Before the גמרא can discuss its laws, it needs to know what this earthenware actually is.

keyTerms.meaning: Hadrianic, connected to the emperor Hadrian

phrases.english: And Hadrianic earthenware.
What is Hadrianic?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the term חרס הדרייני in the משנה.

steps.title: שמואל: the earthenware of Emperor Hadrian
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains that it is the earthenware of הדריינוס קיסר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It is the earthenware of Emperor Hadrian.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by saying the name comes from הדריינוס קיסר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This identifies whose pottery it was but does not yet explain why it is forbidden. רב דימי's report in the next step fills in that detail.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Earthenware of Emperor Hadrian.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל חֶרֶס שֶׁל הַדְרְיָינוּס קֵיסָר
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is the pottery of הדריינוס קיסר.

steps.title: רב דימי explains how the wine-soaked shards were made
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי describes Hadrian's vineyard on untouched soil. Its wine was stored in white jugs that absorbed it, and the jugs were broken into shards that travelers soaked in water to drink.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: There was untouched land that no one had ever worked. Hadrian worked it and planted vines. They put the wine in white jugs, and the jugs soaked up the wine. They broke the jugs into shards and carried them along. Wherever they stopped, they soaked the shards in water and drank.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי gives the full story behind חרס הדרייני. It was pottery so soaked with wine that it worked like portable wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now we see why the shards are forbidden: they hold real wine from non-Jews, which is treated as יין נסך. The wine was so strong that soaking the shards in water produced a real drink.

keyTerms.meaning: Virgin soil, land never worked before

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
There was virgin soil
that no man had ever worked,
he worked it and planted it,
and they put the wine in white jugs,
and the jugs absorbed their wine,
and they broke them into shards
and carried them with them,
and anywhere that they arrived,
they soaked them in water and drank.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands שמואל's short answer with a full description.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Shards from jugs that absorbed Hadrian's wine, soaked in water to make a drink.

steps.title: Our best wine equals their third soaking
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי remarks that our first-rate wine is only as good as the third soaking of those shards.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: Our first-rate wine is like the third soaking of theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי adds a comment showing how strong Hadrian's wine was.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the shards were soaked twice, the third soaking still matched our best wine. This shows how much real wine the pottery held, which explains why the משנה forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Their third, the third soaking of their shards

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
And our first is like their third.
phrases.notes: 'Our first' is our top wine. 'Their third' is the third time the shards were soaked.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי וְרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלָּנוּ כִּשְׁלִישִׁי שֶׁלָּהֶן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine in Hadrianic shards was extremely strong.

steps.title: May the shards be used to prop up a bed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether one may use Hadrianic shards to support bed legs. This is a case of wanting a forbidden object to stay whole for a different, non-forbidden use.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: May one support the legs of a bed with these shards? If someone wants the object to keep existing for a different purpose, is that permitted or forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new question about a practical use of the shards, where the wine inside them gives no benefit at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person gets nothing from the forbidden wine. He only uses the shards as solid props. The real question is general: is it forbidden to want a forbidden item to stay in existence when you use it for something else?

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
What is the law about supporting bed legs with them?

phrases.aramaic: רוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר
phrases.english: One who wants its existence through another matter
is it permitted or forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ מַהוּ לִסְמוֹךְ בָּהֶן כַּרְעֵי הַמִּטָּה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether using a forbidden item for an unrelated purpose, while wanting it to stay intact, is permitted.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle of רוצה בקיומו applies far beyond these shards, to any forbidden item used in a way unrelated to its forbidden part.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a dispute: one of רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן forbids using the shards this way, and the other permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן disagreed. One forbade and one permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by showing that two אמוראים already argued about this exact case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer does not settle the matter by itself, since the two sides disagree and we are not told who held which view. That is why the גמרא next needs a ruling on which side we follow.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
that Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Yochanan disagreed:
one forbade and one permitted,

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is a dispute between רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: The הלכה follows the one who forbids
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows the opinion that forbids using the shards to support a bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows the one who forbade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling: you may not use Hadrianic shards to prop up a bed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though no benefit comes from the wine itself, wanting the forbidden object to stay whole for your own use is forbidden. The ruling settles the question from step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: The law follows the one who forbids

steps.whatToRemember: Hadrianic shards are pottery soaked with non-Jewish wine. Even using them for something unrelated, like propping up a bed, is forbidden, because רוצה בקיומו counts as forbidden benefit.

phrases.english: And the halacha is like the one who forbade.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Using Hadrianic shards to support bed legs is forbidden.

steps.title: Quoting a ברייתא about Jewish wine in non-Jewish jugs
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a challenge by quoting a ברייתא. Its first part says a Jew's wine stored in non-Jewish jugs may not be drunk but may be used for benefit, and it records a testimony about רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא raises an objection. If a Jew's wine was stored in jugs and flagons belonging to non-Jews, he may not drink it, but he may benefit from it. שמעון בן גודא testified before the son of רבן גמליאל that רבן גמליאל drank such wine in עכו, but the חכמים did not accept this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a challenge. It starts quoting a ברייתא, and the part that actually attacks the earlier view comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This first part of the ברייתא is about wine soaked into non-Jewish containers. The vessels have absorbed forbidden wine, so wine stored in them may not be drunk, but benefit is allowed. The story about רבן גמליאל shows that one great teacher was more lenient, but the חכמים did not follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Flagons, a kind of wine container
Forbidden to drink, but allowed to benefit from
They did not agree with him

steps.confusionAlert: This part of the ברייתא is not yet the challenge itself. The real attack comes from the wineskins line in the next step.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
The jugs and the flagons of non-Jews,
if a Jew's wine is stored in them,
it is forbidden to drink but allowed for benefit.
phrases.notes: The wine soaks up forbidden wine that was already absorbed in the walls of the jug.

phrases.english: Shimon ben Guda testified
before the son of Rabban Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: עַל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, שֶׁשָּׁתָה מִמֶּנּוּ בְּעַכּוֹ,
phrases.english: about Rabban Gamliel, that he drank from it in Akko,
but they did not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins quoting a ברייתא to challenge the opinion in Step 8 that permits using the shards to hold up a bed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that permits keeping a forbidden object whole for a different use.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only. The attacking line comes in Step 11.

steps.title: Wineskins may not be made into donkey blankets
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא forbids making donkey blankets from non-Jewish wineskins. The גמרא argues this is exactly a case of wanting a forbidden thing to stay whole for another use, and it is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding wineskins of non-Jews, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says in the name of רבי יהושע בן קפוסאי: it is forbidden to make blankets for a donkey out of them. Here the person wants the wineskin to last for a different use, and the ברייתא teaches that it is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now makes its challenge. Turning a forbidden wineskin into a donkey blanket looks just like using Hadrianic shards to hold up a bed, and the ברייתא forbids it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A wineskin used as a blanket stays whole, and the person benefits from it for something unrelated to the wine. That matches the shards case from Step 7. Since the ברייתא forbids it, the opinion that permits the shards seems to be contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: Wineskins, leather bags for holding wine
He wants it to stay whole

phrases.english: Wineskins of non-Jews:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says
in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Kefusai:
It is forbidden to make blankets for a donkey from them.
But here, where he wants it to stay whole
for a different use,
and it teaches that it is forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דְּרוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר, וְקָתָנֵי דְּאָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in Step 10 and draws out the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion in Step 8 that permits using Hadrianic shards to hold up a bed.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wineskin blanket is a forbidden object kept whole for an unrelated use, just like the shards. The ברייתא forbids it, so the permitting view seems wrong.

steps.title: Pushback: then jugs should not be sold either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. If keeping a forbidden thing whole for another use were the problem, selling non-Jewish jugs should also be forbidden, so wineskins must be different for some other reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to your reasoning, it should be forbidden to buy and sell non-Jewish jugs! So what is different about wineskins, and what is different about jugs?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against the challenge. It points out that jugs are allowed to be bought and sold, even though that also uses a forbidden vessel for another purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wineskin rule came from the idea of "wanting it whole for another use," the same idea would ban trading in jugs. Since jugs are allowed, the wineskin rule must come from a different reason. This sets up רבא's explanation in the next step.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
jugs of non-Jews should be forbidden to buy and sell!
phrases.notes: Jugs like these were commonly traded, so everyone agrees selling them is fine.

phrases.english: What is different about wineskins
and what is different about jugs?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from Step 11 by showing it would prove too much.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the wineskins ברייתא against the permitting view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: If that reasoning were correct, trading in non-Jewish jugs would be forbidden too, and it is not.

steps.title: רבא: wineskins are forbidden because of a separate decree
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that wineskins are forbidden because of a special גזירה. A person might use a piece of the non-Jewish wineskin to patch his own torn wineskin, and the forbidden wine would mix in.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is a decree, in case a person's own wineskin tears and he takes the non-Jewish one and sews it onto his wineskin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why wineskins are different from jugs. The wineskin rule is a special protective decree, not a general rule about keeping forbidden things whole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leather from a non-Jewish wineskin is easy to turn into a patch for a Jewish wineskin. Then the absorbed forbidden wine would touch the Jew's wine. Jugs carry no such risk, so the wineskin ברייתא proves nothing about the Hadrianic shards.

phrases.english: Rava said:
It is a decree, in case his wineskin tears
and he takes it and sews it onto his wineskin.
phrases.notes: He means taking the non-Jewish wineskin and using it as a patch on his own wineskin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: גְּזֵירָה שֶׁמָּא יִבָּקַע נוֹדוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question "what is different?" from Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases: the wineskin ban comes from a separate decree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The wineskin ban is based on the general idea of keeping a forbidden thing whole for another use.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wineskin ban is a special decree against patching, so it says nothing about the shards.
steps.whyThisMatters: This removes the proof against the permitting view, so that view survives the challenge. The הלכה from step 9 still follows the forbidding view, and the next steps explain that view's reasoning.

steps.title: To the forbidding view: why are jugs allowed?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא turns to the view that forbids keeping a forbidden thing whole for another use. According to that view, why is it allowed to buy and sell non-Jewish jugs?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to the one who says that wanting a forbidden thing to stay whole for another use is forbidden, what is different about jugs, which are allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the other side. Trading in jugs also keeps a forbidden vessel whole for another use, yet it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question from Step 12 is now aimed at the forbidding opinion. If that view bans the shards, it seems it should also ban trading in jugs. The גמרא needs a difference between the two cases.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: And according to the one who says

phrases.aramaic: רוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר אָסוּר,
phrases.english: that wanting it to stay whole for a different use is forbidden,
what is different about jugs, which are permitted?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר רוֹצֶה בְּקִיּוּמוֹ עַל יְדֵי דָּבָר אַחֵר אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the jugs question from Step 12 against the opposite opinion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The opinion that forbids using Hadrianic shards to hold up a bed, which is the accepted הלכה from Step 9.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Trading in jugs also keeps a forbidden vessel whole for another use, yet it is allowed. So why are the shards forbidden?

steps.title: In the shards the forbidden wine is still really there
steps.stepSummary: The forbidding view answers: in jugs, nothing forbidden is actually present. In the Hadrianic shards, the forbidden wine is really there, since it can still be soaked out and drunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would say to you: There, in the jugs, the forbidden thing is not actually present. Here, in the Hadrianic shards, the forbidden thing is actually present.
steps.whatsHappening: The forbidding opinion explains why jugs are different from the shards. The difference is whether real forbidden wine is still in the object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary jugs hold only a slight trace of absorbed wine, with nothing you can point to. The Hadrianic shards are soaked with so much wine that travelers soaked them and drank the result, as we saw in Steps 5-6. So keeping the shards means keeping real forbidden wine, and that is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The forbidden thing is actually present and real
It is not there / it is there

steps.whatToRemember: Wineskins are forbidden because of a special patching decree. Jugs are allowed because no real forbidden wine is in them. Hadrianic shards are forbidden even for holding up a bed because the forbidden wine is still really in them.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the הלכה from Step 9 forbids the shards while still allowing ordinary non-Jewish jugs to be traded.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
There, the forbidden thing is not actually present,
here, the forbidden thing is actually present.
phrases.notes: "Here" means the Hadrianic shards, which still hold wine you could soak out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: הָתָם לֵיתֵיהּ לְאִיסּוּרֵיהּ בְּעֵינֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14 and defends the forbidding view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by whether the forbidden substance is actually present.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Jugs and Hadrianic shards are the same kind of case, since both are forbidden vessels kept whole for another use.
steps.terutzMaskana: Jugs hold no real forbidden wine, while the shards still contain real wine, so only the shards are forbidden.

steps.title: Two accounts of the same testimony disagree
steps.stepSummary: One account says the Sages did not agree with שמעון בן גודא's testimony about רבן גמליאל. A ברייתא says they did agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: The earlier account ended: 'and they did not agree with him.' But a ברייתא teaches: wine that comes in non-Jewish flagons may not be drunk but may be used for benefit. שמעון בן גודע testified before רבן גמליאל's son that רבן גמליאל drank from it in עכו, and they agreed with him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets two sources side by side. They report the same kind of testimony with opposite endings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first account, the testimony about רבן גמליאל was not accepted. In this ברייתא, the same witness gives testimony about the same רבן גמליאל, and it is accepted. Both cannot be true as they stand.

keyTerms.meaning: And they raised a contradiction: one source is set against another
Flagons or flasks belonging to non-Jews
They agreed with him (accepted his testimony)

phrases.english: And they did not concede to him.
phrases.notes: This is the end of the earlier account, where the Sages did not accept שמעון בן גודא's testimony about רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
Wine that comes in flagons of non-Jews
is forbidden for drinking but permitted for benefit,
Shimon ben Guda testified
phrases.notes: Here the name ends with an ע. That spelling matters in step 18.

phrases.english: before the son of Rabban Gamliel

phrases.aramaic: עַל רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל שֶׁשָּׁתָה מִמֶּנּוּ בְּעַכּוֹ,
phrases.english: about Rabban Gamliel, that he drank from it in Akko,
and they conceded to him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a ברייתא against the ending of the earlier account of שמעון בן גודא's testimony
steps.kashyaTarget: The report that the Sages did not agree with שמעון בן גודא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source says the same testimony was accepted, so the two reports contradict each other

steps.title: Only the group disagreed, while the son agreed
steps.stepSummary: 'They did not agree' means the rest of the group. רבן גמליאל's son did agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'they did not agree with him' mean there? His whole group did not agree, but his son did agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by explaining who 'they' refers to in each source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first account means the rest of the Sages did not accept the testimony. The ברייתא's 'they agreed' refers to רבן גמליאל's son, who was the one being spoken to. So both reports are true about different people.

keyTerms.meaning: His group or company (the other Sages)

phrases.english: What is 'they did not concede to him'
that it says there?
His whole group did not concede,
phrases.notes: He means the rest of the Sages who were present.

phrases.english: but his son did concede to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי לֹא הוֹדוּ לוֹ דְּקָאָמַר הָתָם
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting who is meant: the group versus the son
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources speak about the same people agreeing or not agreeing
steps.terutzMaskana: The Sages as a group did not agree, but רבן גמליאל's son did

steps.title: Two different men named Guda
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: גודא spelled with an א and גודע spelled with an ע are two different people.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: גודא is one person and גודע is a different person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another way to remove the contradiction, this time based on the spelling of the name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first account names the witness גודא, with an א. The ברייתא names him גודע, with an ע. If these are two different witnesses giving two different testimonies, then the reports never contradicted each other.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: introduces another answer

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers. Either the group disagreed while the son agreed, or there were two different witnesses (גודא and גודע).

phrases.english: If you want, say:
Guda is separate, and Guda is separate.
phrases.notes: The first name is spelled with an א and the second with an ע, so they are two different men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, separate answer to the contradiction of step 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different people: the two sources are about two different witnesses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources describe the same witness and the same event
steps.terutzMaskana: גודא and גודע are different people, so there is no contradiction

steps.title: Defining a hide torn at the heart
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's item עורות לבובין and brings a ברייתא that defines it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'and hides torn at the heart.' The Rabbis taught: What is a hide torn at the heart? Any hide that is torn opposite the heart and cut round like a window opening, and has a drop of blood on it, is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next item in the משנה and starts explaining what counts as an עור לבוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא gives a clear definition. The tear must be opposite the heart and cut round like an opening, and there must be a trace of blood on it. A hide with all these signs is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Hides with a tear opposite the heart
A drop or trace of blood

phrases.english: And hides torn at the heart.
The Rabbis taught:
What is a hide torn at the heart?
Any that is torn opposite the heart
and cut round like a kind of window opening,
and has a trace of blood on it
is forbidden,
